chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah al-Mad'ani from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The stray animal is not eaten by anyone except those who are astray, if they do not announce its finding.

key_terms.اَلضَّالُّونَ: Those who are astray (referring to the finder who misappropriates it)
key_terms.اَلضَّوَالُّ: The stray animal (specifically one that has wandered off and is not being guarded)
key_terms.يُعَرِّفُوهَا: To announce/proclaim its finding (to notify potential owners)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a finder of a stray animal to be considered guilty of misappropriation?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration by Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the condition for liability in consuming a stray animal (*al-dhawal*), linking the act of consumption directly to the failure to announce (*ta'rif*) the find. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on public notification as a mechanism to protect property rights and prevent unjust enrichment, distinguishing between mere possession and culpable misappropriation.
